report:
The current selection theorem, sharp centering dichotomy, joint varying-density theorem, and central zero-lower-mass factor construction are established within their stated scope. They provide substantive restricted S05 progress for genuine L1 densities belonging to no Lp, p>1. They do not solve the unrestricted programme or establish a moving singular-reference theorem. Earlier acceptance labels and source-reading receipts were not used as mathematical evidence.

The radial calculation is correctly normalized. With L=(ρ+uα)'=m+α(1−ψ)^(α−1)(1−m), positivity gives 0<L<1 and L'>0. The actual annular Monge–Ampère measure has cumulative flux Q=L^k. Its endpoint fluxes are zero and one. Bounded truncation locality therefore establishes the non-pluripolar probability measure, rather than merely a formal determinant; the canonical pole contributes no atom. The density extends smoothly across infinity with value 1−α. Near the pole its radial measure is comparable to t^(−1−k(1−α))dt, while −uα is comparable to t^α. Consequently its first moment is finite exactly when (k+1)α<k. The density’s exponential growth relative to smooth volume proves failure of every Lp with p>1.

The product prerequisites also hold. Dimension and bounded-product expansion give the binomial product formula, so bounded small-mass potentials on X0 imply v_−(H)=0. A closed positive h0 would instead have fixed bounded Monge–Ampère mass, proving genuine nonclosedness. Smooth projective equations produce product normalization b/∫gκ^k. Multiplicative approximation, scalar monotonicity and reciprocal homogeneity extend this formula to positive continuous g. Applying it to min(qα,j) establishes the exact task-defined threshold b. The supplementary truncation sandwich also handles an arbitrary smooth reference volume. Actual pullback truncations give the unbounded threshold equation and finite mass b.

Bounded positive-exponent comparison is applicable without a bounded mass property: both backgrounds are strictly positive, a sufficiently negative constant is a strict barrier, and every qj is smooth, positive and bounded. The radial regularity proof is sound. Symmetric convolutions of the convex logarithmic profile decrease with their scale, allowing local bounded Bedford–Taylor convergence. The flux equation first gives finite-radius smoothness; the displayed origin and infinity integral equations give Lipschitz extensions and then smooth bootstrap. Smooth maximum comparison therefore proves wλ,j≥uα and monotonicity in j.

The greatest-family identification can be made explicit without importing an additional approximation theorem. The bounded separated product solution is dominated by the task’s greatest qj-solution; that greatest solution is consequently bounded, and bounded uniqueness identifies them. Every qα exponential subsolution is also a qj exponential subsolution because qj≤qα. Thus the greatest qα-solution lies below every separated approximant. Conversely, dominated density convergence and the annular flux identities make the decreasing separated limit an actual qα-solution, which the greatest solution dominates. These two inequalities establish equality on the full product. The limiting equation has total mass one on Y and zero initial flux; convergence of total masses alone is not being substituted for product convergence.

Dinew’s stability hypotheses are satisfied on the closed projective factor. The potentials are canonical, supremum-zero and full mass. For fixed α, their measures are eventually dominated by 2qακ^k, and the task-granted measure convergence becomes actual total-variation convergence on Y. This common finite measure vanishes on every pluripolar set. Stability gives L1 and base capacity convergence along every exponent sequence, hence for the whole family. Uniform cumulative-flux convergence gives uniform derivative convergence on finite logarithmic-radius intervals; the L1 limit fixes their constants. The uniform exponential tail estimate extends local uniform convergence through infinity. Pullback gives the claimed product L1 and local uniform convergence, without asserting product-capacity convergence.

The finite-moment centering argument retains the scalar error. The exact probability identity and e^r≥1+r give ∫wλqα≤0. A fixed positive-measure annulus, the normalized smooth-volume L1 bound and wλ≥uα bound aλ uniformly. The exponential difference quotient has integrable negative and positive bounds, so every subsequential constant satisfies Mα+a=0. Integration by parts gives the displayed explicit constant; its pole boundary term vanishes precisely below the stated moment threshold. At and above that threshold, the nonnegative normalized difference quotient and Fatou’s lemma force aλ→∞, while scalar convergence gives λaλ→0. Thus the divergent unscaled error is fully compatible with convergence of the normalization scalars.

The joint theorem requires no relation between αj and λj. On any compact parameter interval inside (0,1), the stated radial estimate supplies one integrable density g dominating all qδ. Dominated convergence proves density convergence. The canonical normalized L1 bound gives smooth-volume tails bounded by C/R; absolute continuity of the integral of g then controls their g-mass uniformly. Splitting at R=λ^(−1/2) proves ∫(1−e^(λv))qδ→0 uniformly without assuming a first moment against g. The exact probability equation therefore yields e^(λjaj)→1, and the equation measures converge in total variation while remaining bounded by 2gκ^k. Dinew applies again. Below the limiting moment threshold, (−uα+)g is integrable and the centering constants converge to −Mα. At the boundary or above it, Fatou applied with the varying densities forces aj→∞, including approaches from below. The local uniform upgrade remains uniform in the parameter.

The selection characterization is intrinsic within the separated sector. Every projective critical subsolution dominating qακ^k has mass at most one by closed bounded truncations and at least one by domination. It therefore has that exact full measure. Full-mass uniqueness makes it uα+d, interpreted canonically also at poles. Hence uα is the greatest critical subsolution with supremum at most zero; when Mα is finite, uα−Mα is the greatest one with qα-mean at most zero. This proves an order criterion rather than merely asserting agreement of cluster limits. No uniqueness of arbitrary critical potentials on the nonclosed product follows.

The reference remains zero. For every stretching factor t, the genuine competitor uβ−Ct with β>α satisfies (uβ−Ct)/t≤uα, including the common canonical pole. Its pullback proves the exact all-scale E_env definition. This does not establish ordinary bounded type relative to zero, nor use an unrestricted converse involving envelope equality. Exponential weights are zero at canonical −∞ values, and the prescribed density measure gives the pole fiber no mass.

The named example is nonvacuous. The quotient action is free and proper, its indicated strip is compact, and the resulting threefold is connected. In the trace-concentration contradiction, Lamari applies to the possibly nonclosed smooth form Cω−Bδ. Canonical compactness supplies a nontrivial limit. After adding local smooth potentials, Siu applies to positive closed currents, not to the nonclosed background current. The lifted analytic set would contain the accumulating deck-translated hyperplanes and hence an open set, a contradiction. Both averaging constructions have the stated degree bounds; the curve evaluation map is a submersion and fixed-j smoothing is sufficient. The complementary cofactor blocks and Schur estimate yield unbounded positive-root volume. The supplied direct AM–GM/Stokes argument then converts this into smooth admissible potentials with mass tending to zero, without using the older unproved dual-volume formula. Fiber integration gives V0=24π, so k=2 gives b=240π. For example α=1/2 supplies a concrete non-Lp finite-centering case; α=2/3 realizes the divergent-error boundary.

Source conventions are compatible: Tosatti–Weinkove potentials are multiplied by 2π; Dinew potentials are divided by two, with equivalent capacities obtained by convex rescaling of bounded tests. BGL’s applications are invariant under positive operator rescaling. Harmless wording corrections are needed in older notes: the abstract v_− hypothesis supplies bounded small-mass potentials, whereas smooth ones require the concrete factor proof; equality up to constants should be written without subtracting common −∞ values. The supplied later supplements already resolve these points and the geometric Lelong normalization. The two noted BGL v1 typographical slips do not enter the bounded applications. No substantial mathematical repair is required. Ancillary corollaries in the frozen author source are outside its expressly stated use as the central factor prerequisite.

passages.statement: For locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions on an open subset of C^d, Bedford–Taylor mixed products are positive, closed, symmetric and multilinear, and are continuous under pointwise decreasing sequences with locally bounded limits. Such functions are quasi-continuous, and their top-degree products do not charge pluripolar sets. [Bedford–Taylor, Theorem 2.1, Corollary 2.2, Theorem 3.5 and Theorem 6.9](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~ebedford/PapersForM655/BTNewCapacity.pdf).

On a compact complex manifold with smooth strictly positive Hermitian background θ and smooth positive volume dV, every nonzero nonnegative f in Lp(dV), p>1, and λ>0 admit a unique bounded canonical θ-psh solution of MAθ(u)=exp(λu)f dV, without a bounded mass assumption. For bounded θ-psh u,v, if MAθ(u)≤c MAθ(v) on {u<v} for a constant 0≤c<1, then u≥v. [Boucksom–Guedj–Lu, Section 4, Lemma 4.2 and Theorem 4.5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2406.01090v1).

On a ball U in C^d, let h be a bounded quasi-continuous obstacle and let p be its upper-regularized plurisubharmonic envelope, defined using domination outside a pluripolar set. If p is bounded, its Bedford–Taylor measure satisfies (dd^c p)^d({p<h})=0. [Boucksom–Guedj–Lu, the bounded envelope argument in Theorem 2.9 and its local use in Lemma 4.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2406.01090v1).

For a smooth semipositive real background ω and bounded canonical ω-psh u,v on an open set, the corrected bounded products satisfy MAω(max(u,v))≥1_{u>v}MAω(u)+1_{u≤v}MAω(v). If u≥v, then 1_{u=v}MAω(u)≥1_{u=v}MAω(v). [Guedj–Lu, Lemma 1.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2106.04272).
passages.quote: Let u, v, ϕ be bounded ω-psh functions in U ⊆ X.

passages.statement: For a smooth real (1,1)-form θ on a compact complex n-fold, without requiring dθ=0, nonnegative pairings ∫θ∧Θ≥0 against every smooth strictly positive dd^c-closed (n−1,n−1)-form Θ imply the existence of a real distribution χ such that θ+dd^cχ≥0 as a current. [Lamari, Lemma 3.3](https://www.numdam.org/article/AIF_1999__49_1_263_0.pdf).

A real distribution on an open subset of C^d whose complex Hessian is positive has a unique locally integrable plurisubharmonic representative. The cone of locally integrable plurisubharmonic functions is closed in L1loc, and every subset bounded in L1loc is relatively compact in that topology. [Demailly, I.5.8–5.9](https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf).

passages.statement: For a positive closed current T of bidimension (p,p) on a complex manifold and c>0, the geometric Lelong upper-level set {x:ν(T,x)≥c} is analytic and has complex dimension at most p. Geometric Lelong numbers are invariant under holomorphic coordinate changes. [Demailly, Théorème 4.14 and Corollaire 2.2](https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/lelong.pdf), [III.8.5](https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf).

On a compact Kähler manifold (Y,ω), two canonical full-mass potentials in E(Y,ω) with the same non-pluripolar Monge–Ampère measure satisfy φ=ψ+C for a real constant C. [Dinew, Theorem 1.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0804.3407v1).

Let (Y,ω) be compact Kähler with ∫ω^d=1. Let μ be a finite measure vanishing on all pluripolar sets, and let φj,φ belong to E(Y,ω), all with supremum zero and MAω(φj),MAω(φ)≤μ. Weak convergence MAω(φj)→MAω(φ) implies φj→φ in L1 and in ω-capacity. [Dinew, Theorem 1.3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0804.3407v1).
passages.quote: Furthermore in this case the functions φj converge to φ in capacity.
